Use case: sketch-to-render. ONE separate photoreal full-body running Border Collie image, not a multi-pose sheet. Input1 is accepted photoreal Frame041 and the PRIMARY EDIT TARGET. Edit it by one small forward instant to Frame042, preserving exact individual, camera, scale, lighting and studio. Input2 is Frame042 guide for the gathered-airborne phase, mild spinal flex, fixed floor and general whole-body height; for closing the cycle, the actual photographic paw layout in inputs1 and3 has priority over exact sketch joint coordinates. Input3 is accepted Frame001, the EXACT NEXT-FRAME ENDPOINT. Frame042 should be an almost matching photographic pose just one small instant before this endpoint, rather than changing the dog or returning to a different pose. Any additional photographs are neighboring pose references, not extra dogs. Produce exactly1536x1024, fixed left-facing strict side view. Whole nose, four paws and tail visible. Same black-white long-haired athletic adult, white blaze/muzzle/chest/paws and tail tip, semi-prick ears, brown eye. Matte light-gray studio, same floor y850 and soft contact shadow. Keep torso center around x800, same body proportions. Guide shapes become realistic rounded flesh and fur, with no visible guide lines. Four connected canine limbs, separate paws, normal shoulder/elbow/wrist and hip/stifle/hock; never fused, missing or twisted limbs. Near means left side visible to camera, far means right side. Changes in body height, spine flex and pitch must carry the whole skeleton. Head gaze remains nearly level through small neck compensation. Ears, coat and tail respond mildly to motion. Clean sharp realistic action photo, no motion blur, no text or accessories. The pose should progress only one small instant from a neighboring image, while fulfilling this guide's paw contacts and targets. Target coordinates are control suggestions; use natural limb articulation rather than square sketch edges.
